Interpreting \(i l j\) as \(i\mid j\) (i divides \(j\)), let

\[
Q=\sum_{\substack{1\le i,j\le 2009\\ i\ne j,\ i\mid j}} a_i a_j.
\]

We will show the maximum is \(\frac5{11}\).

---

### 1. Longest divisibility chain

If

\[
x_1\mid x_2\mid \cdots \mid x_m
\]

with distinct positive integers, then each step at least doubles the number:

\[
x_{k+1}\ge 2x_k.
\]

Thus

\[
x_m\ge 2^{m-1}x_1\ge 2^{m-1}.
\]

Since \(x_m\le 2009\) and

\[
2^{10}=1024\le 2009<2048=2^{11},
\]

we must have \(m\le 11\).

This bound is attainable, for example by

\[
1\mid 2\mid 4\mid 8\mid \cdots \mid 1024,
\]

which has \(11\) elements. Hence the maximum length of a divisibility chain in \(\{1,2,\dots,2009\}\) is \(11\).

---

### 2. Color the numbers by chain length

For each \(i\in\{1,2,\dots,2009\}\), define

\[
c(i)=\text{maximum length of a divisibility chain ending at }i.
\]

Then \(c(i)\in\{1,2,\dots,11\}\). Moreover, if \(i\mid j\) and \(i\ne j\), then a maximal chain ending at \(i\) can be extended by \(j\), so

\[
c(j)\ge c(i)+1.
\]

Therefore any two numbers \(i,j\) with \(i\mid j\), \(i\ne j\), have different colors.

Let

\[
S_k=\sum_{c(i)=k} a_i,\qquad k=1,2,\dots,11.
\]

Then

\[
S_k\ge 0,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^{11} S_k=1.
\]

Because every pair contributing to \(Q\) lies in two different color classes,

\[
Q\le \sum_{1\le p<q\le 11} S_pS_q.
\]

But

\[
\sum_{1\le p<q\le 11} S_pS_q
=\frac12\left(\left(\sum_{k=1}^{11}S_k\right)^2-\sum_{k=1}^{11}S_k^2\right)
=\frac12\left(1-\sum_{k=1}^{11}S_k^2\right).
\]

By Cauchy’s inequality,

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{11}S_k^2\ge \frac{1}{11}\left(\sum_{k=1}^{11}S_k\right)^2=\frac1{11}.
\]

Thus

\[
Q\le \frac12\left(1-\frac1{11}\right)=\frac5{11}.
\]

---

### 3. Achieving the bound

Set

\[
a_i=\frac1{11}
\]

for

\[
i=1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128,256,512,1024,
\]

and set all other \(a_i=0\). These \(11\) numbers form a divisibility chain, so every two distinct ones are comparable by divisibility.

Hence

\[
Q=\binom{11}{2}\left(\frac1{11}\right)^2
=\frac{55}{121}
=\frac5{11}.
\]

Therefore the maximum value is

\[
\boxed{\frac5{11}}.
\]
